newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end off 23-mth low, may fall more.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end off 23-mth low, may fall more.

text.p: Singapore's benchmark Straits Timex Industrials Index (STI) ended just above a 23-month low on Monday following a heavy sell-off on New York on Friday and amid rumours of funds switching out of equities.
"It is difficult to persuade anyone to buy today," said one gloomy broker with a large local bank.
The 30-share STII closed at 2,034.64, down 33.84 points or 1.64 percent, just above an intraday low of 2,031.07 points.
The last time the index was this low was on April 20, 1995.
Dealers reported an all-pervasive bearish mood and said some analysts were rumoured considering downgrading some sectors.
"We'll probably do more selling tomorrow," said the broker.
"If it doesn't hold at this level, the prospects are bad," said another. "The next stop for the STI would be 1,900 points."
Several property shares rose, including Wing Tai and DBS Land, which had been sold off heavily on Friday ahead of government measures to curb subsidies for public housing.

But these gains were more than outweighed by falls in industrial blue chips. Of the STI component stocks, marine-based SembCorp and drinks firm Fraser & Neave led the fall, both down 40 cents to Singapore $6.60 and S$11.00 respectively.
